novel_features.name: Conflict verdict engine
novel_features.description: One command answers 'am I double-booked?' across every account, and refuses to give a confident all-clear over partial or stale data.
novel_features.rationale: Implements a reviewed verdict contract (fresh-or-downgrade, busy-only, tz-normalized, mirror-aware) across three live accounts — no cache, no single-account blind spots.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this whenever asserting schedule truth to a human — its downgrade semantics make the answer citable.

novel_features.name: Open-slot enumeration
novel_features.description: Ranked open windows of a requested duration across all accounts, computed from live freebusy under the same busy semantics as conflicts.
novel_features.rationale: Google has no find-a-time endpoint; interval inversion across tz-normalized sources is exactly what ad-hoc arithmetic gets subtly wrong.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when proposing meeting times — 'open' carries coverage evidence, not guesswork.

novel_features.name: Safe-mutation contract
novel_features.description: Writes take an etag precondition and return the pre-image plus a structured inverse operation, so every change is cleanly reversible and race-safe.
novel_features.rationale: If the human edited the event mid-flight, the write fails cleanly instead of clobbering; undo evidence rides in the response.
novel_features.example: google-calendar-pp-cli events update primary evt123 --account ads --start 2026-08-19T15:00:00-06:00 --if-etag "abc" --json
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for any mutation an agent must be able to echo-with-undo to its principal.

novel_features.name: Stateless change sweep
novel_features.description: Everything that moved, appeared, or was cancelled across all accounts since a caller-held watermark — deletions included.
novel_features.rationale: The CLI holds no state; the watermark is the caller's, so change detection stays lawful under a no-local-cache rule.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run between full sweeps to catch mid-day schedule movement cheaply.

novel_features.name: Manifest reconciliation
novel_features.description: Diffs live calendar reality across all accounts against the approved calendars.yaml — new, missing, or permission-drifted calendars become findings.
novel_features.rationale: The manifest is the governance root; silent drift would quietly poison every downstream verdict.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Schedule this as hygiene; run it before trusting any multi-account verdict after account changes.

novel_features.name: Recurring-series deviations
novel_features.description: Instances of recurring events that moved or were cancelled in a window — the routine-deviation surprises, isolated.
novel_features.rationale: No endpoint lists deviations; comparing originalStartTime vs start and cancelled status across accounts is in-process logic.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use in look-ahead sweeps: deviations from routine are the highest-yield surprise class.

narrative.headline: The multi-account Google Calendar layer for agents that must never surprise a human.
narrative.value_prop: Role-scoped OAuth profiles (a read-only account literally cannot write, by token), a conflicts engine whose all-clear carries coverage evidence, and mutations that are idempotent, etag-guarded, undo-bearing, and structurally incapable of emailing attendees. Built as the calendar substrate for an always-on personal-assistant agent; useful to anyone juggling multiple Google accounts from scripts.
narrative.auth_narrative: Auth is per-profile installed-app OAuth: you supply a client.json from your own Google Cloud project, then run auth --account <name> once per account. Each profile declares a role — readonly profiles request calendar.readonly only, so write scopes never exist on that token. Tokens live in the configured token dir, never in the repo.

quickstart.comment: One browser round per account; the profile's role decides which scopes are requested
Confirm every profile authenticated and show each token's role
Merged calendar list across all accounts — the raw material for your manifest
Tomorrow across every account, with per-source freshness stamps
The verdict: double-bookings, suspected mirrors, and coverage ('checked N of M')

troubleshoots.symptom: invalid_grant or token expired shortly after setup
troubleshoots.fix: The OAuth app is still in Testing mode — publish it to Production in the Google Cloud console, then re-run auth for each account
Enable the Google Calendar API on the Cloud project that issued your client.json

troubleshoots.symptom: conflicts reports 'checked N of M sources'
troubleshoots.fix: A source failed or served stale evidence — run doctor and manifest check before trusting an all-clear
By design: attendee-bearing events are never mutated by this CLI; change them in the Calendar UI

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI whenever schedule truth spans more than one Google account: conflict sweeps, availability questions, agenda merges, and gated calendar writes performed on a human's behalf. It is deliberately stateless — every answer is a live read with freshness evidence, so it suits agents whose answers must be citable.

recipes.title: Reversible reschedule
recipes.command: google-calendar-pp-cli events update primary evt123 --account ads --start 2026-08-19T15:00:00-06:00 --if-etag "etag-from-read" --json
recipes.explanation: Fails cleanly if the event changed since you read it; response carries the pre-image and inverse op.
